root_idea.summary: The root centers on an established origin or firm base, together with things gathered into a stable whole.
root_idea.development: Its imagery begins with the firmly rooted tree and extends to becoming established, accumulating wealth or resources, strengthening dominion, and figuratively acquiring durable honor or standing. Some derived uses apply the idea to collecting debts, provisions, people, or water from a well.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized noun citation form أَثْلٌ.

senses.definition: A tamarisk or tamarisk-like tree, characterized as firmly rooted.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrence names the tree in a list of vegetation; the classical description compares it with the ṭarfāʾ and emphasizes its established root and useful wood.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take root or a foundation; to become firm, established, or firmly rooted; of dominion, to become great.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form I, generally intransitive; the application to dominion includes becoming established or great.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a person of high rank or nobility, to be or become ancient in origin or long-standing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I vocalic variant used of rank or nobility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To give something a root or firm foundation; to make it stable, established, lasting, or great.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II causative use, applied especially to dominion, property, or other things made durable.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impose or make a duty binding on someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic interpretation of the construction أَثَّلَ عَلَيْهِ; the lexical explanation compares imposing a payment or obligation with establishing it against someone.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To increase wealth or property, or put it into a good and sound condition; intransitively, to become abundant in wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II transitive and intransitive uses concerning wealth or property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reinforce or enlarge a party by adding men to it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a person or party as the object of multiplication.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To collect debts against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is the person against whom the debts are accumulated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clothe one's family in excellent clothing and treat them well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A benefactive household use of Form II.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become firmly fixed or established.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive Form V development of the notion of acquiring or possessing a firm root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become collected or gathered together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V intransitive use describing things coming together as a whole.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To obtain provisions for oneself, especially after a period of need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The acquired item is أَثْلَة, understood here as food or provisions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acquire or accumulate a source, stock, or fund of wealth or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form V use of taking wealth for oneself as a lasting source or reserve.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take wealth or property from other people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form V construction in which the wealth is obtained from people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To dig a well for oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The well is treated as a newly acquired source of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collector of wealth or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression فُلَانٌ أَثْلُ مَالٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Honor, reputation, or inherited grounds for respect, including ancestral merit or standing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use; impugning or detracting from someone's أَثْلَة means attacking their reputation or claims to honor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The root, foundation, origin, or source of a thing, person, or wealth; a stock or fund.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used broadly of anything with an origin or foundation, including a source of property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Victuals or provisions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate nominal use, synonymous with مِيرَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The goods, furniture, and utensils of a house or tent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers collectively to household equipment and possessions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Apparatus, accoutrements, implements, or similar equipment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of equipment assembled for a purpose, such as winter preparations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Glory, honor, dignity, nobility, or high rank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use; both أَثَالٌ and أُثَالٌ are reported vocalizations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wealth or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative nominal use distinct from the related sense of glory or rank.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place where trees of the arāk kind grow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports this sense with a possible textual confusion or mistranscription for أَثْل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Abundant, luxuriant, or long hair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing the quantity, luxuriance, or length of hair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rooted, founded, firmly established, permanent, or of ancient origin; figuratively, established in honor, rank, or wealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-result adjective applied to things, dominion, glory, nobility, and property.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Prepared, arranged, disposed, or put into a good and proper condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A result-state adjective describing something made ready or set in order.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Taking for oneself or acquiring a source, stock, or fund of wealth or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participial form describes accumulation of property as a personal reserve or lasting fund.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I becoming rooted or established.
Dominion becoming great is covered in the same Form I branch.
Ancient origin or long standing of high rank.
Form II making firm, founded, or lasting.
Contains establishment/greatness and the distinct obligation construction.
Intransitive abundance of wealth is included in the wealth branch.
Acquiring a source or stock of wealth.
Collecting wealth as a personal fund.
Tree meaning represented by the Quranic noun sense.
Nominal idiom for a collector of wealth.
Singular tree noun covered by the Quranic tree sense.
Reported place of growth of arāk trees, with textual uncertainty noted.
Rooted, permanent, ancient, or figuratively established.
Prepared or put into good condition.
Acquiring a personal fund of wealth.

cautions: The Quranic occurrence is securely located by QAC at 34:16:12. A classical printed citation rendered as xxxiv. 15 is not used to infer an alternate modern Quran location.
Botanical descriptions identify أَثْلٌ as tamarisk or a closely related tamarisk-like tree and vary in their precise classification.
The reported أَثِيلٌ sense meaning a place of tree growth is retained separately because its source notes that the word may be a textual mistranscription for أَثْل.
